countries.name: China
countries.what: Chinese stocks jumped Friday after a rare intraday state media readout said policymakers would do more to stem the market's decline. The CSI 300 rose more than 4% to 4,063.06, and chip stocks such as SMIC and Cambricon led a record 17% one day gain in the CSI Semiconductor index (CNBC; Wind). October industrial profits rose 20.1% (NBS via CNBC).
countries.for_you: No action. A one day jump on a policy promise is hope, not a trend, and the US tariff proposal still hangs over PDD. Chinese ADRs have no buy points; watch whether FXI holds the move next week. The chipmakers that led are not US tradable.

countries.name: Gulf (Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar, Iran risk)
countries.what: Kuwait's army said Nov 26 that two Italian nationals were killed in alleged Iranian attacks, which Iran denied, and Israel said it could strike Iran without US help (CNBC). Brent was about $96.51 early Friday and US crude rose 3.0% to $85.75; Saxo had Brent over $97. OPEC meets Sunday Nov 29 (Forex Factory).
countries.for_you: DAL is on the long term scan buy list at its 82.60 point, and oil near $97 is the main risk to that call: keep any DAL buy small and wait until after Sunday's OPEC meeting. CVX has a ready pullback and oil helps it, but there is no swing setup.

countries.name: South Korea
countries.what: The KOSPI rose 4.34% to 4,915.68 on Friday and the tech heavy Kosdaq rose 8.13% (CNBC). Saxo said reports that authorities may expand the market stabilization fund helped.
countries.for_you: No action. EWY's confirmed break down still stands until it closes back over its range on 1.5x volume, so still no puts on Korean names. One strong day after a 6% drop is a bounce until it holds.
